newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada buying C$552 mln of armor from GM.
newsitem.headline: Canada buying C$552 mln of armor from GM.

text.p: The government of Canada awarded a C$552 million contract on Thursday to General Motors of Canada to build 240 new armored personnel carriers (APCs), Defense Minister Doug Young announced.
The contract also contains options for the future purchase of up to 411 more APCs, turreted eight-wheeled vehicles that can drive on roads or across country and ford rivers.
The company, wholly owned by General Motors Corp, will start delivering the vehicles in January 1998 and finish in December 1999.
Funding for the program was provided for in previous federal budgets, a news release said.
An accompanying background statement said the cost of the project would be C$800 million in 1995-96 dollars, spread over four years.
This would include not just making the APCs but also initial spare parts support, ammunition and project management cost.

It added that if all the options for the extra 411 APCs were exercised over the next seven years the total price for 651 APCs would be at most C$2.04 billion in 1995-96 dollars, including the parts support, ammunition and management costs.
Public Works Minister Diane Marleau said in a joint statement with Young that the contract represented 16,000 man years of employment.
The APCs, which will have a 25-mm cannon, will be based on a similar design as the Coyote reconnaissance vehicle which GM Canada is currently delivering to the Canadian forces.
Common designs would result in savings in training, operations and maintenance costs, the background statement said.
